newsitem.title: EL SALVADOR: Mexico's TV Azteca buys Salvador TV channel.
newsitem.headline: Mexico's TV Azteca buys Salvador TV channel.

text.p: Mexican business tycoon Ricardo Salinas Pliego announced Friday he had bought a Salvadoran television network and planned to open two appliance stores in Guatemala as part of a major expansion into Central America.
Salinas, who controls Grupo Elektra as well as Mexico's number two television network TV Azteca, said he planned to invest more than $200 million in Central America over the next few years.
Salinas said he had bought 75 percent of El Salvador's TV 12 for $12 million and planned to spend another $10 million in El Salvador opening Elektra stores in coming months.
Eventually Salinas said he planned to spend "over $100 million" buying stakes in television channels in the region and another $100 million opening around 50 Elektra stores.
Another $5-6 million would be invested in setting up a local beeper company, the Mexican businessman added.
Salinas said he had chosen El Salvador to start television operations because it was "a country which has shown an incredible recovery after the (civil) war".
TV 12 will now move to 24-hour programming and start including Azteca-produced soap operas in its schedules.
